markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's OWN Investigation Record rows (e.g. the mitosis stage order they set, the chromosome count in each daughter cell, a cell they built).
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine rows from their own record; wording need not be exact.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('I built cells') with no actual record cited.

markingScheme.criterion: States that mitosis makes two new cells (daughter cells) that are identical to the parent and have the same number of chromosomes.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'It makes more cells' with no mention of two identical cells.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a purpose of mitosis in a body: growth, healing wounds, or replacing damaged/old cells.
markingScheme.accept: Any one of growth, repair/healing, replacement.

markingScheme.criterion: Names mitosis (cells dividing/copying) as the process that repairs the knee, by replacing damaged cells.
markingScheme.accept: 'cells divide to make new skin cells'; 'mitosis'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'It just heals' with no cell division.

markingScheme.criterion: Says one bacterium makes more bacteria by copying itself and splitting in two (binary fission / asexual reproduction), with no partner needed.
States that the number keeps doubling (1, 2, 4, 8...) so a few can become millions quickly, e.g. every 20 minutes in good conditions.
markingScheme.accept: 'doubles', 'again and again', quoting the 20-minute figure or a doubling sequence.

Any two of the three Explain points are achieved.
All three Explain points are achieved: own records quoted, two identical daughter cells with the same chromosomes, and a purpose of mitosis.

levels.descriptor: None of the three Apply points is achieved.
Any one of: mitosis repairs the knee / bacterium splits in two / numbers keep doubling.
Any two of those three Apply points.
All three Apply points: mitosis replaces damaged cells, a bacterium splits in two by itself, and the number keeps doubling.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together - independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above. Spelling or grammar slips only cost a mark when they stop the meaning being clear.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed.
Main meaning understandable but organisation, precision or science words are weak.
Clear and logical, with correct words such as cell, nucleus, mitosis, chromosome or bacteria.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses using the point-by-point markingScheme (award each point independently unless it states dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands - do not invent extra criteria. Each rubric row's 'source' says which question's marks it equals; never award those marks twice. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept'; do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Check claims about the student's own results against the Investigation Record rows, not just their prose. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
